title: It's that simple
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: If you want to meet the people who matter to you, where would you go?

What do you admire in other people, I asked? Who do you want near you? Who do you want in your team? Where is your center? Is it material things, or time, or freedom, or experiences, or people who are motivated and good energy that you grow with?
A student said: the people who spark my intuition are the ones who are polarizing, so different from the herd. Someone who doesn't care what people think and carves their own path. It is magnetic.
How do you find the people you want to meet, I asked? The mentors, the teammates, the people for long relationships? A student said: you be the person you want to be.
I asked again: how do you find people like you? A student said: do you go to the places where those people hang out? I said: very good. It's that simple.

I told how I met a friend of thirty years at a bookstore. She pulled a book off the shelf in the philosophy section, and I asked why she was interested in it. We talked for twenty minutes. A shared interest in that book started a friendship that has lasted thirty years.
If you want to meet people who are artistically oriented, go to art galleries, I said. You are not going to meet them at a loud club on a Friday night.
A student added: if you are always on the bar street, the people you hang out with are the ones who are always at the bars. Is that who you want to be friends with? It is the same in business.

I said the same goes for clients. When you walk into a store and feel the energy, you think: I love this store. Those are the clients you want to work with, because they already have momentum in that direction.

If you go to a store where so many things are wrong, I said, you will try to fix them, and they won't, because they don't get it. But where you feel the magic and feel congruent, they will speak your language.

If a river is coming down, you don't stop the river, I said. You go with the water. You can channel it. When I meet people, I want people who already have direction, a little purpose, momentum, a work ethic, values and integrity.
A student said: the golf courses that care about how their property looks are the ones that want to work with us, and they are easier to sell and close.
That is a statement you make, I said. We work with the kind of customers who care about this. It is part of your branding too.
Who already has momentum in your direction?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you admire in other people, and where your center is: things, time, freedom, experiences.
Write where the people you want to meet spend their time.
Write one place you will go this month.
Write the kind of customer who already has momentum in your direction.
Write the one-line statement: we work with people who care about ___.

check.q: How did a student say you find the people you want to meet?
choices: Go to the places where those people hang out

check.q: Where did I meet a friend of thirty years?
What did I say about a river?
choices: You don't stop it, you go with the water

recap: Go where the people you want already are. Work with those who already have momentum.
